latestNews.details: The Bruins have acquired JJ Peterka from the Mammoth for the No.23 overall pick in 2026 and a 2028 first-round pick.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Peterka's time in Utah lasted just one mediocre season after the 24-year-old was acquired by Boston for the No.23 overall pick in 2026 and a 2028 first-round pick on Friday. Peterka is just one season removed from a 27-goal, 68 point campaign in 2024-25 but took a step backwards in Utah last season with just 25 goals and 47 points in 82 games played. He is expected to play a key top-six role in Boston's lineup this upcoming season.

latestNews.details: Lindholm will be a healthy scratch for Saturday's game vs. Slovakia.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Lindholm has not registered a point and is a minus-2 through two games for Sweden, so he'll come out of the lineup Saturday vs. Slovakia. Marcus Johansson will draw into the lineup to replace him in the lineup, but Mika Zibanejad will move up to replace him on the second line.

latestNews.details: Pastrnak (undisclosed) is on the ice for warmups and is expected to return to the Bruins lineup on Tuesday.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Pastrnak has been incredibly resilient for the Bruins, playing all 82 games in the previous three seasons, and will now return to the lineup after missing five games due to an undisclosed injury. The 29-year-old elite Czech forward has 29 points (11G / 18A) in 25 games, factoring in on 37 percent of Boston's goals before his injury.

latestNews.details: Mittelstadt will not play against the Devils on Tuesday.

latestNews.fantasyDetails: Geekie exited Saturday's game to tend to a personal matter and subsequently did not play on Sunday, but he will re-enter the lineup on Tuesday against the Detroit Red Wings. The 27-year-old Geekie is having another excellent offensive season for the Bruins, with 41 points (25G / 16A) in 45 games. That said, he has just two assists in his last nine contests.

latestNews.details: Hagens is expected to be a healthy scratch for Game 4 vs. Buffalo.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Hagens playoff debut has started with three scoreless games and has led to Lukas Reichel expected to replace him in Boston's lineup for Game 4 vs. Buffalo. The 19-year-old Hagens joined the Bruins after a strong season at Boston College (NCAA) and has one assist in five appearances with the Bruins across regular season and the playoffs.

latestNews.details: Jeannot (rest) is expected to be back in the Bruins lineup on Tuesday.

latestNews.details: Lindholm (rest) is expected to be back in the Bruins lineup on Tuesday.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Lindholm was a healthy scratch due to rest-related purposes for Boston's previous game but will return to the lineup for Game 82 vs. New Jersey on Tuesday. latestNews.details: Boston has acquired Will Borgen from New York for a 2027 2nd round pick and a conditional 2028 3rd round pick.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Borgen has become a reliable bottom-four defenseman in recent seasons and will bring his talents to the Boston Bruins after being acquired in a trade. The 29-year-old Borgen averaged 18:03 time-on-ice, recording 15 points (5G / 10A) and a +3 plus/minus in 75 games last season.

latestNews.details: Zadorov (undisclosed) will play in Game 5 in Buffalo.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Zadorov was a game-time decision heading into Game Four on Sunday, but ended up playing in the blowout 6-1 loss to the Buffalo Sabres, recording four hits and 17 penalty minutes in 19:20 time-on-ice. The hard-hitting 31-year-old defenseman is likely battling the same ailment he has had over the past week, making his status uncertain again for Game Five on Tuesday.

latestNews.details: 2-year, $4,500,000 contract with the Boston Bruins. Expires 2028 (UFA).
Aspirot (illness) will return to the Bruins lineup on Saturday.
Lohrei is expected to be a healthy scratch for Game 4 vs. Buffalo.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Lohrei has struggled mightily in Boston's opening three games to start the playoffs and is expected to head to the press box for Game 4 vs. Buffalo as Jordan Harris enters the lineup. Lohrei appeared in 73 regular season games for the Bruins but has been battling throughout the playoffs with zero points, and a -4 plus/minus despite averaging 14:14 TOI per game.

latestNews.details: Swayman will start the Bruins' season opener vs. the Rangers.
latestNews.fantasyDetails: Swayman is entering his seventh season in the Bruins' crease and will unsurprisingly start Boston's season opener on Tuesday when they host New York at TD Garden. The 27-year-old is coming off an impressive bounce-back campaign in 2025-26 that saw him finish fourth in the NHL in wins (31) alongside a 2.71 GAA and .908 SV%. He will host the Rangers on Tuesday, who are coming off a forgettable 2025-26 campaign which saw them finish eighth in the Metropolitan Division with a record of 34-39-9.

latestNews.details: DiPietro has been assigned to Providence (AHL).
latestNews.fantasyDetails: With Jeremy Swayman returning from his stint with Team USA at the Olympics, DiPietro will return to the AHL after a brief one-game stint as Joonas Korpisalo's backup. The 26-year-old DiPietro is having a marvelous season in the AHL with Providence, posting a dazzling 1.76 GAA and .938 SV% in 30 games (22-6-0).

We’re bringing you the latest updates and news around today’s Boston Bruins line combinations so you can see where each player is expected to fit in their next game. Knowing the Bruins line combinations can help with building a sharper bet slip, finding value in your NHL fantasy hockey league, or staying informed as a fan.

You can also review which players are expected to be used on the power play and penalty kill units, along with players who are unavailable due to injury or being scratched.

The Bruins lines today may change before their next game, so check back regularly for the latest Boston lineup updates ahead of puck drop.

Bruins Line Combinations

Below, we’ve broken down each of the Boston Bruins line combinations by position group. Here you can see all four forward lines, three defensive pairings, and the current goalie depth chart.

Forward

The Bruins forward lines give you a clear look at how Boston is structuring its attack at even strength. From the first line through the fourth, this section helps show which players are being grouped together and how the coaching staff is balancing scoring, checking, speed, and matchup responsibilities.

Forward combinations can shift based on injuries, recent performance, special teams usage, or the opponent, so checking back before puck drop is the best way to stay current on Boston’s expected setup.

Defense

The Bruins defensive pairings show how Boston is organizing its blue line for the next game. This section helps identify which defensemen are expected to play together, who may be trusted in tougher defensive minutes, and which pairings could be counted on to move the puck out of the zone.

Defensive combinations can change based on matchups, injuries, and special teams needs, making this a useful section to monitor throughout the season.

Goalies

The goalie depth chart gives you a quick look at Boston’s expected starting goaltender and backup for the next game. Since starting goalie decisions can influence betting markets, fantasy hockey lineups, and overall matchup expectations, this is one of the most important areas to check before puck drop.

Projected starters are based on the latest available information, but goalie confirmations can change throughout the day depending on morning skate reports, coach availability, and team announcements.

Power Play

A team’s power play units are important to track because they show which players are being placed in premium offensive situations. For Boston, the power play section highlights the skaters expected to receive top man-advantage minutes and the secondary group that follows behind them.

Power play deployment can be especially useful for fantasy hockey and betting research, since players on the top unit often have more chances to generate shots, assists, goals, and points.

Penalty Kill

The penalty kill section shows which Bruins players are expected to handle shorthanded minutes. These roles are generally given to players who can defend well, anticipate plays, win battles, and limit dangerous chances while Boston is down a skater.

Penalty kill usage can also provide helpful context for ice time, defensive responsibility, and matchup deployment, especially for players who may not always stand out offensively.

Injuries

Injuries can have a major impact on the Bruins line combinations, especially when a regular contributor is unavailable. When a player is injured or scratched, it can force changes across multiple forward lines, defensive pairings, and special teams units.

This section helps track which Boston players are currently unavailable and how those absences may affect the projected lineup.

Using Boston Bruins Lines for Betting and DFS

Using the latest Bruins lines can help you make more informed decisions for sports betting, daily fantasy, and season-long fantasy hockey. Line combinations can reveal which players are receiving stronger offensive opportunities, who is moving up the lineup, and which skaters may be gaining more valuable ice time.

Before placing a bet or setting a DFS lineup, it can be useful to review Boston’s forward lines, power play units, goalie confirmation, and injury updates. These details can help you better understand how the Bruins may approach their next matchup.

The power play units are especially important to watch, as players featured on the top unit are often placed in the best position to generate offense. Tracking those assignments can help identify potential value before the market fully adjusts.

Whether you are looking for betting angles, fantasy hockey value, or a clearer understanding of the Bruins lineup tonight, this page gives you a reliable starting point before puck drop.
